description: The paper that renders itself: PortableDoc's new diff and filetree blocks — scaffolded by bp scaffy run in 9 ms with zero tokens, then grown into real renderers on all three surfaces — demonstrate themselves on their own birth commits, alongside the honest W7 benchmark and the convenience verdict.

blocks.text: PortableDoc Code Story — the blocks that render their own birth

content.value: On 2026-07-17 the PortableDoc grammar grew from 46 to 48 block types. The two newcomers — diff and filetree — were scaffolded by
with parity on every surface at birth, then grown into real renderers. This paper is written in them: the diff block below shows the commit that created the diff block.

blocks.text: The diff block, showing its own birth

was added by hand — one word). Hunk headers stay verbatim and dim, git file headers become bold path sub-headers, and the +/− prefixes carry the semantics without color.

content.value: Per charter D83, the numbers are kept apart: the engine's scaffold time (deterministic text ops, zero tokens), the ASSERT CMD gate cost (go build/test, pnpm, vitest — a CI cost that runs whether or not a scaffold produced the code), and the grow time (the judgment work of writing real renderers, metered from this wave's own task ledger).

rows.value: 11 ops per block: 2 files created, 9 injections — skeleton, wiring, test parity on all three surfaces
One tier injection; the second same-tier run is structurally refused — filetree was a one-word hand-edit (D79)
ASSERT CMD gates: first go build/test + pnpm install/build + vitest — CI cost, never conflated into scaffold time
The same gates on warm caches
Real diff/filetree renderers on the shared chat-row helpers; full pdrender suite green, chat golden parity 8/8
Byte-identical Elixir/JS renderers, 48×2 golden regen, all gates (mix 157, react 260, tsc clean)

content.value: The point, plainly: the skeleton, the cross-surface wiring, and the test parity were free and byte-consistent on every surface — the engine reproduced an independent prior scaffold byte-for-byte. All the time went where the judgment is: growing starters into real renderers. And one honesty rule stands:
no measured pre-scaffy baseline exists for adding a block type

— W6 scoped the add-block-type duel to A-vs-C, so this paper makes no hand-vs-scaffold comparison for this chore. For duel-measured A-vs-B numbers, see the W6 benchmark paper at /papers/scaffy-benchmark.
This wave doubled as the deferred convenience fixture: if building two blocks back-to-back exposed real friction, Scaffy would earn new machinery. It mostly didn't.

items.value: The lived chain is two commands — add-block-type folded the parity leg in v2 — and it ran fine as a documented shell recipe. The one real bleed, the structurally refused second same-tier classify (exit 5, nothing written), is a REANCHOR limit that binds regardless of orchestration: no chain or meta-command fixes it. The honest fix — a classify-block-type redesign that appends into the tier list instead of re-anchoring the opener — was backlogged as scaffy-backlog-classify-append-redesign, with this wave as its fixture, and has since shipped: the 2026-07-17 append-friendly restructure turned tiers.ex's ~w sigils into plain string lists, the op into a bare INSERT AFTER FIRST, and a second same-tier classify into an independent clean insert.
Multi-line vars are engine-impossible by design and were not needed; batch vars buy nothing over the shell recipe; value-capture stays deferred with zero new instances.

The corpus now tells the truth about itself: dry-run always reports ok:false on the two golden EXISTS asserts (cosmetic — read duration_ms), growing a renderer past its starter stales the parity golden and the mandatory regen step is documented, and classify-block-type carries the pairing law plus the same-tier hand-edit recipe.

content.value: Scaffy scaffolded the blocks; the blocks now render the scaffold. Every diff and filetree you just read was drawn by the code this paper describes.
